text: Mouse ES cell-derived clones and chimeras often show fetal growth abnormalities—over- or under-weight offspring with elevated neonatal mortality and morbidity. Because imprinted genes regulate fetal growth, improper epigenetic reprogramming of cultured cells is suspected. This study examined two growth-regulatory imprinted genes, Igf2 and H19, in mouse ES cells grown under growth-restricted conditions and after in vitro aging. Serum-depleted media (starvation) and high cell density (confluence) increased expression of both genes and caused aberrant methylation profiles of differentially methylated regions at key regulatory sites of Igf2 and H19. These results confirm that growth-constrained culture alters methylation of imprinted gene regulatory domains and their expression patterns, suggesting epigenetic factors may contribute to loss of developmental potential in ES cell-derived offspring.
